description: A look at the Thanksgiving week slate and all of its fixings you need in time for Turkey Day
body:
A look at the Thanksgiving week slate and all of its fixings you need in time for Turkey Day
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:00 pm ET

            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL has cooked up something special for this year's Thanksgiving. For the first time, a Thanksgiving Eve game was added to the Thanksgiving week slate. It's essentially an appetizer for Thursday's triple-header feast, with the dessert coming Friday with the Black Friday game.  Each game has storylines big enough to fill any plate. To keep up with everything, we've provided a rundown of how to follow the games in real time. We've also included the major thing to know for each matchup. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bears (8-2) at Lions (8-2)When: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 1 p.m. ETWhere: Ford Field -- Detroit, Michigan TV: CBS | Stream: fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Bears -2.5, O/U 55.5 (via DraftKings)What to know: While he's had a lot of success in Chicago, Ben Johnson is 0-2 against Detroit, his former team. Johnson's former boss, Dan Campbell, has won four straight games against Chicago, seven of his last eight in the series and has a 7-3 overall record against the Bears. Coaches aside, this is a matchup between two of the NFL's hottest teams. The Bears have won five straight games, while the Lions enter Thursday with a six-game winning streak. The winner of this game will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North. 
It'll be especially interesting when the Lions' fifth-ranked offense is on the field against Chicago's sixth-ranked defense. Jahmyr Gibbs, who is one touchdown away from breaking Barry Sanders' NFL record for the most touchdowns by a player before his 25th birthday, should have his moments. He's facing a run defense that is just 25th in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Eagles (3-7) at Cowboys (5-6)When: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ETWhere: AT&T Stadium -- Arlington, TexasTV: Fox | Stream: fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Cowboys -8.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings)What to know: Dallas is a sizable favorite, but there are several reasons to believe that the Eagles are ripe for an upset. The Cowboys were 10-point favorites when they were upset by then-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers back in Week 5. Dallas lost that game to a backup quarterback (rookie Jalon Daniels), and they'll face another backup Thursday in Joe Milton III, who used to play for America's Team. Milton just won his first career start Sunday against the Steelers. He made several clutch plays, including his third-down conversion to DeVonta Smith that iced the game. 
If Dallas wins on Thursday, it will be the first time it's won back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys' inability to string together consecutive wins is yet another reason why Philadelphia could successfully play the role of spoiler. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chiefs (8-2) at Bills (9-1)When: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETWhere: Highmark Stadium -- Orchard Park, New YorkTV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Bills -3, O/U 50.5 (via DraftKings)What to know: This game will be billed as the latest chapter in the Josh Allen-Patrick Mahomes rivalry. Overall, the Allen-Mahomes series is tied up at five wins apiece, which makes Thursday night's game a rubber match. Allen is 0-4 against Mahomes-led teams in the playoffs, but he has a 5-1 record in regular-season starts against Mahomes that includes five straight victories. Both quarterbacks will look to put on a show, but the winner of this game will likely come down to which supporting cast outperforms the other. On paper, the Chiefs have a few advantages, most notably their second-ranked scoring defense that will look to exploit Allen's Kryptonite: turning the ball over. Allen has thrown nine interceptions this year, including five in his last four games. 
It'll be interesting to see how the Chiefs' young players fare in a big-time environment, especially Emmett Johnson, Kansas City's rookie running back, who has tallied consecutive 100-yard rushing performances while filling in for injured starter Kenneth Walker III. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Broncos (8-2) at Steelers (6-4) When: Friday, Nov. 27 | Time: 3 p.m. ETWhere: Acrisure Stadium -- Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania TV: None | Stream: Prime Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Broncos -3, O/U 37.5 (via DraftKings)What to know: This game is pretty simple. If the Steelers are going to pull off an upset, they're going to have to take advantage of Denver's suspect run defense and third-down offense. If they can't do either of those things, the Broncos will more than likely hand them their third straight loss. Jaylen Warren was having a monster season for Pittsburgh until he and the rest of the Steelers' offense hit a wall over the last two weeks. Pittsburgh's lack of depth at receiver has led defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage, leaving little running room for Warren and back mate Rico Dowdle. 
A positive for Pittsburgh is the emergence of wideout Max Hurleman, who caught a team-high six passes for 61 yards and a score against the Eagles. Plus, the recent return of Roman Wilson and the possible return of Michael Pittman, who hasn't played since Week 4, are bright spots. The Steelers will also have DK Metcalf after the league decided not to suspend him following his ejection during Sunday's loss in Philadelphia.

description: Steelers players spoke favorably about Aaron Rodgers after his release, while team sources reportedly corroborate
body:
Steelers players spoke favorably about Aaron Rodgers after his release, while team sources reportedly corroborated portions of the quarterback's explosive criticism of Mike McCarthy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While Aaron Rodgers was publicly scorching Mike McCarthy, several Steelers watched their now-former teammate inside the locker room following Wednesday's practice. It was a surreal moment in a truly bizarre 24 hours for the Steelers, who ultimately released Rodgers after his criticism of McCarthy. Pittsburgh announced late Tuesday night that Rodgers would be inactive against the Broncos and would be replaced by Mason Rudolph. Rodgers, during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, accused McCarthy of being late and sleeping through meetings, not watching film of opponents the week of games and saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" in the locker room at halftime during Sunday's eventual loss to the Eagles. McCarthy has since confirmed his Packers snafu in a press conference, calling it an embarrassing moment.Anonymous team sources corroborated Rodgers' claim that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, according to The Athletic."He's not lying," an unnamed player said. Several players were interviewed at their locker, including tight end Pat Freiermuth, rookie quarterback Drew Allar, rookie receiver Germie Bernard, and veteran wideout Marquez Valdes-Scantling, who was also Rodgers' teammate in Green Bay. Each spoke favorably about Rodgers. 
"I think he's the best player to ever play this game as his position," Valdes-Scantling said. 
Rodgers said that Freiermuth informed him Tuesday night of the Steelers' decision to deactivate him. "I was just checking in on a close friend," Freiermuth said. 
Allar started to address questions about Rodgers but stopped after he was waived off by veteran safety DeShon Elliott. 
"For me, it's kinda sad to see, because I have a lot of respect for Aaron," Allar said. "I've learned a lot from him since he's been here. I think I'm gonna leave it at that and just with Aaron the best." 
Bernard shared a message that McCarthy told the team earlier in the day. "Just gotta come together. It's all about unity," he said. "Coach told us today that the best teams are player-led, and we have all the veterans, we have all the talent in the world to do that. So we just have to lean on each other." Bernard also exuded confidence in Rudolph, who will make his first start of the season Friday against the Broncos. 
"Mason is a great quarterback," he said. "We have complete trust in him, and he has complete trust in us. We've just got to go out there and believe in what he can do so we can get it done."

title: Mike McCarthy responds to Aaron Rodgers, confirms QB gave him 'ultimatum:' 'I know how to win' - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy responded to Rodgers' tirade against him
body:
McCarthy responded to Rodgers' tirade against him
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:24 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the wake of Aaron Rodgers' sudden benching, the now-former Pittsburgh Steeler went scorched Earth on coach Mike McCarthy, accusing him of everything from incompetence to negligence. Facing a litany of embarrassing allegations, McCarthy has now shared his side of the story.McCarthy began his press conference by stating that he wouldn't reveal any specifics about his private conversations with Rodgers. Asked why McCarthy was the right person to lead Pittsburgh through this messy situation, McCarthy bluntly referred to his overall track record as a coach."I know how to win, and that's the facts," McCarthy replied. "This is my third program. I plan on winning here because of the men and because of this organization."Explaining the decision to bench Rodgers, which ignited this firestorm, McCarthy said the quarterback gave him an "ultimatum." At that point, McCarthy felt the need to make a change.
"It was a process that went on throughout this week," McCarthy said. "We got to a point. We talk about communication and things like that. There was an ultimatum made clearly outside of his job description. So, it was my decision to bench him."Rodgers claimed that no one informed him of McCarthy's decision to bench him, and he only found out when tight end Pat Freirmuth alerted him to the news. McCarthy refuted Rodgers' story, saying there were multiple attempts to reach him."I know there were continuous efforts to reach Aaron, and I know there was communication with his agent," McCarthy said. "I don't know exactly the specifics on the other side of the conversation."
ESPN reported that McCarthy "has the full support" of the Steelers organization and "will remain their head coach." However, Pittsburgh hasn't released any official statement or responded to the allegations in any way yet. McCarthy confirms '1-2-3 Packers' momentAsked directly about Rodgers' accusation that McCarthy broke down a team huddle at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Eagles by saying, "1-2-3 Packers," McCarthy conceded that it was an "embarrassing moment." He cited working "long hours" as an explanation for the slip-up. However, McCarthy added that he and Rodgers had a "difference of opinion" about how the locker room received it.Speaking of the locker room, Rodgers also alleged that McCarthy has made little effort to connect with the players, particularly those on defense. The Steelers coach said he met with the team's leadership council and felt like both sides came to an understanding.
"I'll just say that I came from a player council meeting," McCarthy said. "I thought it was a meeting that was very direct and very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind. Comments that brought discussion to the forefront. I'm proud of our leadership. More importantly, I loved the urgency coming out of that meeting."McCarthy added that some of those things "should've been talked about earlier" and presented a "growth opportunity" for himself and the team."Probably should have had more dialogue earlier in the process when I first arrived here," McCarthy admitted. "I do respect Mike Tomlin and his career here and the things that are in place. I don't have a throw-the-baby-out-with-the-bathwater philosophy. When you have situations that create honest and direct conversation, there are good things that come out of that."
When the Steelers hired McCarthy to replace Mike Tomlin, one of the first things he did was advocate for the return of Rodgers at quarterback. At the time, McCarthy didn't hesitate when asked about the idea of re-signing the veteran quarterback."Definitely. I don't see why you wouldn't," McCarthy said. "I have spoken to Aaron, and so that's really where we are there. I was able to sit back and watch the games. I watched most of the Pittsburgh games on TV, and I thought he was a great asset for the team."Once a McCarthy-Rodgers reunion was finalized, Pittsburgh hoped that duo had a little more magic left after their run to a Super Bowl XLV championship with the Green Bay Packers. Instead, the relationship has turned toxic in a matter of months.
It was bad enough when the offense was sputtering and Rodgers was arguing with McCarthy on the sideline, but that seems rather rosy compared to where things stand now. On his way out the door, Rodgers asserted that players don't respect McCarthy as Pittsburgh fights to stay in the AFC playoff race with Mason Rudolph under center.
        
            
                Aaron Rodgers unleashes on Mike McCarthy: Unpacking everything Steelers QB said after benching
                
                    Bryan DeArdo                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
What Rodgers said about McCarthyIn an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show," Rodgers teed off on McCarthy and his alleged lack of professionalism since taking over in Pittsburgh.First, Rodgers claimed he found out about his benching through tight end Pat Friermuth. In fact, Rodgers said McCarthy still hasn't spoken to him about the decision. From there, Rodgers asserted that McCarthy was an absentee coach in the lead-up to the Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
"Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting," Rodgers said. "Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again, and less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room, like nothing happened. Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting.   "Friday, he doesn't come to the walkthrough. We only have a walkthrough really on Friday. Doesn't come to the first walkthrough. Doesn't come to protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don't have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly. And then comes to Sunday, when obviously we struggled, and the product wasn't great, and you know there were some guys early on that didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys that Mike didn't want to get another defense.  "So a lot of those guys, you know, he kind of already lost a lot of those guys. And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime."
Ultimately, Rodgers said the "nail in the coffin" came at halftime of the loss. The ex-Steelers quarterback said McCarthy went from a "rambling" speech to breaking the team down with, "1-2-3 Packers." At that moment, Rodgers said he felt McCarthy completely lost the locker room.Now Pittsburgh is left preparing to play the Denver Broncos on a short week as the team tries to pick up the pieces from a humiliating Wednesday for the entire organization.

body:
Arsenal are still up there after falling just short in the 2026 final, while key injuries dent PSG's three-peat bid and Jose Mourinho has Real Madrid surging
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026

        The Champions League season is still in the league phase, but we can start to look ahead into the new year with some teams performing better than others. Real Madrid, PSG and Arsenal are in great form, but there are also other teams that might improve in the second part of the season, when things will become more serious and everything will be decided. Let's go around Europe to see which are the best teams in the tournament right now. Here are the 10 teams capable of winning it all, ranked.10. AS RomaCan you imagine AS Roma challenging for the trophy? Well, it's very difficult, if not impossible, but this seems like a dreamy season for the Giallorossi so far, and their striker Donyell Malen is in stunning form. Gian Piero Gasperini was able to completely shape his team in his second season at the club. What a journey.9. Manchester CityThe Citizens are playing a season without knowing what will come next. The potential verdict coming in the near future and the fact they also replaced a manager like Pep Guardiola at the beginning of this campaign can definitely have an impact on their current performances and I don't see them potentially going for the title. For sure, they have the potential to bounce back and regain some confidence, considering the players they have available.8. InterThe Italian team didn't have their best start of the season but they are one of those sides that can drastically improve in the second half of the campaign, if they learn how to defend again. Inter played in two of the last four Champions League finals and have some experienced players who can help them to achieve that target again. It won't be easy, but they are one of those candidates that we need to keep in our minds in the second part of the season.
7. Atletico MadridNever underestimate a team coached by Diego Simeone. They are behind right now and unlikely to be a challenger for the trophy at the end of the season but we should always consider Atletico Madrid in the conversation. To make that happen, some things must change in the winter transfer window to improve their current squad. Not impossible, but also not very likely at this stage.6. LiverpoolSpeaking of teams that need to improve to reach the level of the top four at least, Liverpool is one of them. They replaced their coach in the summer and there are still too many ups and downs so far. Andoni Iraola is a coach with the experience and the capabilities to reach the later stages of the tournament, but it's difficult to imagine they can challenge the other big teams, at least based on what they have shown so far.5. Bayern MunichI would rate the German giants in a much higher position but we also need to understand they currently have their two best players, at least on paper, injured or not at their best. Harry Kane will miss at least three months of action while the future of Jamal Musiala is still uncertain due to his physical conditions. The big question is when and how this duo will be back, but Bayern can definitely be a challenger for the trophy.
4. BarcelonaThe Blaugrana are always part of this conversation, especially considering Lamine Yamal's ambitions to win the trophy and potentially win the next edition of the Ballon d'Or. Hansi Flick's target is to replicate his domestic success of the last two years in Europe.3. Real MadridJose Mourinho is back in action and Real Madrid are in great form, but more than anything, so are his players. Both Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham are probably playing their best season so far since they joined the Spanish giants, while Vinicius Jr is also hoping to reach his top form in the shortest time possible. They look particularly solid this season.2. PSGI would still consider them the leading candidates to win the tournament again, particularly after lifting the trophy in the past two editions, beating Inter and Arsenal in the respective finals. However, their chances have been significantly dented by injuries. Both Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are expected to miss the remainder of the season and, even if the club brings in replacements during the winter transfer window, losing two players of such importance is likely to have a major impact on their chances of retaining the title.
1. ArsenalThis has to be their season. Having finally won the Premier League last year, they now need to build on that success and consolidate their status at home, while also making a serious push for European glory. After coming so close last season, only to lose the 2026 final against PSG, they have every reason to believe they can go all the way.

body:
A look at some of the most iconic performances from Turkey Days of the past

        NFL halftime shows have evolved since the beginning of the league. What began as marching bands and local high school bands has now turned into full productions.Thanksgiving has featured big performances from top artists since 1997, when Reba McEntire performed at the first Salvation Army Red Kettle Kickoff halftime show, which kicks off the Salvation Army's annual Red Kettle Campaign and encourages fans to give back to those in need. This year, three games will be played on Thanksgiving Day. Bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+, Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills face off at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.Wu-Tang Clan will perform in Detroit, Miranda Lambert in Texas, and the Goo Goo Dolls in New York. This doesn't include the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, where U2 will perform at halftime. 
Here is a look at 10 of the most memorable Thanksgiving halftime show performances: Creed, 2001
You can't mention Thanksgiving halftime shows without mentioning Creed's Texas performance. There were silk aerial dancers, a man flying through with giant wings, mimes, choir singers and many other elements that left people with a lot of questions.Dolly Parton, 2023
A 77-year-old Dolly Parton took the stage in a Dallas Cowgirl costume and proved why she is a country music legend. She performed "Jolene," "9 to 5" and made a medley with Queen's "We Will Rock You" and "We Are The Champions." Any Dolly performance is automatically iconic, and this was no different. 
Reba McEntire, 1997
Since she kicked off the tradition of Thanksgiving halftime shows, McEntire has to make the list. She performed at Texas Stadium with a choir and dancers, along with the Cowboys cheerleaders. The country music legend performed on a star stage and wore Cowboys blue. Destiny's Child, 2004
Any Destiny's Child performance is automatically memorable. The Texas natives were an obvious choice for a Texas halftime show. The trio performed "Lose My Breath" and "Soldier" from their final studio album. A marching band and cheerleaders joined their performance. Mariah Carey, 2005
Mariah Carey may be the queen of Christmas, but she also knows how to put on a great Thanksgiving performance. The pop diva performed "Shake It Off" and "Don't Forget About Us" from her album The Emancipation of Mimi. The Ford Field performance also included a marching band and dancers. Carey began the performance being carried by men in football uniforms. People on the field created an "M" and "C." 
Carrie Underwood, 2006
Carrie Underwood has become an NFL staple, as the singer of Sunday Night Football's theme song. Her ties to the NFL also include a Thanksgiving halftime show performance. She sang her hit song "Before He Cheats" and "We're Young and Beautiful" in Texas, with an elaborate backdrop and silk aerial dancers.Sheryl Crow, 2005
Sheryl Crow brought down the Texas house with her rock vibes on Thanksgiving Day. She performed "Good Is Good" and her biggest hit "If It Makes You Happy." With acrobatic dancers and ribbon twirlers, her exciting performance became an instant classic. Jonas Brothers, 2008, 2022
The Jonas Brothers are one of the biggest boy bands of the early 2000s and 2010s, and their performance was a hit with any Disney Channel fans. The Jonas Brothers performed in 2008, singing hits including "Lovebug" and "Burnin Up." They became the first-ever repeat performers when they returned in 2022, singing new hits including "Only Human." Both performances were at the Cowboys' home.
Kelly Clarkson, 2007
The American Idol winner and Texas native performed in front of the Cowboys' home fans. She performed "Walk Away," "Never Again," and "Since U Been Gone" in front of Dallas cheerleaders, pyrotechnics, and flashing lights. Jack White, Eminem, 2025
Jack White headlined last year's Lions Thanksgiving halftime show and surprised fans by bringing out Eminem. White opened with "That's How I'm Feeling" before introducing Eminem, who performed "Till I Collapse." The two Detroit natives were a hit with the Ford Field crowd.

title: Steelers release Aaron Rodgers following criticism of Mike McCarthy: Possible landing spots for QB - CBS Sports
description: Rodgers will get a chance to finish his career elsewhere if he chooses
body:
Rodgers will get a chance to finish his career elsewhere if he chooses
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Aaron Rodgers' time with the Pittsburgh Steelers has ended after he heavily criticized Mike McCarthy hours after Pittsburgh made him inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos. Shortly after his criticism, the Steelers announced that they had released the quarterback, and he officially hit the waiver wire Wednesday afternoon. Any team can sign Rodgers until 4 p.m. ET on Thursday. If no team claims him by then, he will become a free agent. Rodgers, 42, had re-signed with the Steelers in hopes of finishing his career with a successful reunion with McCarthy, his coach with the Packers from 2006-18. Instead, Rodgers will look to finish his career elsewhere. It appears that Rodgers' breakup with Pittsburgh was the result of a disagreement between Rodgers and McCarthy over play-calling duties. The Steelers had been running more hurry-up offense in recent weeks. In that situation, the play-calling duties are more split between Rodgers and quarterbacks coach Tom Arth. McCarthy clearly wanted a more collaborative approach. 
Rodgers said that his desire to handle more of the play-calling duties was a byproduct of, in his words, McCarthy being late and sleeping through team meetings. Rodgers said that McCarthy said, "1-2-3, Packers!" at halftime during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Rodgers said that was essentially the last straw and decided to address his concerns with McCarthy this week. Those discussions led to the end of Rodgers' time with the Steelers, who will face the Broncos on Friday with Mason Rudolph under center. While the Steelers move ahead, Rodgers will now try to figure out his next move. Here are five possible landing spots for Rodgers, who did not say whether he still plans to retire after this season, given what has transpired over the last 24 hours. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New England Patriots At this point, there are only two realistic possibilities for Rodgers if he wants to be a starter. The best option of the two is New England, who recently lost Drake Maye to a potentially season-ending injury. The Patriots have lost three out of their last four games, but they still have a decent shot at making the playoffs, especially if the Steelers fall off without Rodgers. New England has a chance to get back over .500 this week if they can defeat the 1-9 Chargers in Los Angeles. Would Rodgers make much of a difference? He would be an upgrade over Tommy DeVito, but the odds of the Patriots actually defending their AFC title are slim either way. The Patriots have struggled on both sides of the ball this year and have four games left against teams with winning records. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baltimore RavensBaltimore is in a total freefall. After a 2-0 start, the Ravens have lost seven straight games and are sitting by themselves in the AFC North cellar. Lamar Jackson's season-ending injury essentially ended Baltimore's season. The Ravens recently acquired Jacoby Brissett, who played relatively well in close losses to the Chargers and Texans. There's a chance, however, that the Ravens may decide to add Rodgers to their quarterback room to see if he can provide a further spark. Baltimore would also gain an advantage from an intel standpoint if they signed Rodgers. The Ravens have two upcoming games against Pittsburgh, their longtime rival. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ersThis is mostly a nostalgia move. Rodgers is a California native who grew up a diehard 49ers fan. The 49ers famously passed on him in the 2005 NFL Draft, and Rodgers has never been shy about his desire to show his childhood team they made a big mistake. In this scenario, Rodgers would have the chance to go home and play for his childhood team, albeit in a backup role. He also could serve as a mentor for Brock Purdy, who is having an MVP-caliber season. Given the 49ers' injury history, Kyle Shanahan probably wouldn't mind having a backup with Rodgers' experience. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay Packers Another nostalgia move that would be largely ceremonial. While his exit from Green Bay wasn't perfect, Rodgers is currently on good terms with both Matt LaFleur and Jordan Love. Unlike his mentor, Brett Favre, Rodgers could close out his career with the team that shaped his NFL legacy. 
It wouldn't be the perfect ending, but a return to Green Bay — even as a backup — would give Rodgers some semblance of closure to what has been a Hall of Fame career. Retirement Rodgers can also retire, which may or may not come on his terms. If he goes unclaimed and no one signs him this season, Rodgers would have to wait to see if another team comes calling this offseason, which might not happen. It's very possible that Rodgers wouldn't have played this season if the Steelers didn't offer him a chance to return. Rodgers wouldn't be the first professional athlete to retire that way. In fact, there are a host of great players across numerous sports who have had their careers end in a similar fashion, albeit without the scorched-earth interview. Players seldom get the John Elway retirement where they get to ride off into the sunset with a championship. More often than not, players are told when the ride is over. That can happen to Rodgers, or he can choose to shape the narrative by calling it quits on his own terms.

        The San Diego Padres have agreed to terms with veteran left-handed reliever JoJo Romero on a free-agent contract, ESPN reports. It's a three-year deal worth $21 million, according to The Athletic.Romero, who'll be going into his age-30 campaign in 2027, is coming off a solid 2026 campaign for the St. Louis Cardinals and, after the trade deadline, the Milwaukee Brewers. 
Those numbers don't include Romero's work in the postseason during the Brewers' run to the World Series title. In 8 playoff innings for Milwaukee, Romero pitched to a 1.13 ERA with 11 strikeouts against only one walk. 
Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Romero as the No. 31 free agent in the 2026-27 class. Here's part of that write-up: "An appendectomy split Romero's season in two. He was great during the Brewers' postseason run and has been one of the game's better lefty relievers for four years now. His sinker/sweeper attack is plenty good enough that Romero does not have to be sheltered against righties."For his career, Romero has a 3.51 ERA/119 ERA+ with a K/BB ratio of 3.86 across parts of seven MLB seasons. Over the last three seasons, Romero has a 2.91 ERA, which comes to an ERA+ of 140. He served as closer for the Cardinals for part of the 2025 season, which means he has late-inning experience. Across his 252 career relief appearances, Romero has limited left-handed batters to a slash line of .202/.281/.301. 
Last season, the Padres returned to the playoffs in large measure because of their dominating bullpen. However, their most crucial setup man, lefty Adrian Morejon, is presently a free agent and thus may be bound elsewhere this offseason. Romero is no Morejon, but he does profile as a useful bullpen presence, especially if the gains he enjoyed while on the Brewers' watch prove to be sustainable.

title: Rams vs. Packers prediction: Can Green Bay continue success with deep ball? Will L.A. overcome injuries? - CBS Sports
description: Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground
body:
Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground attack in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve showdown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:41 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL game, the Los Angeles Rams play host to the Green Bay Packers. The Rams enter this game coming off their bye week, and they are incredibly banged up on offense. Puka Nacua is likely out for the year, as is Terrance Ferguson, after they each underwent surgery on lower-body injuries. Davante Adams remains out with his hamstring injury as well. The Rams will need their defense and their running backs to carry the day against a tough Packers team.Green Bay is also coming off the bye, but is getting healthier for this game as Micah Parsons will make his season debut after tearing his ACL toward the tail end of last season. Parsons returning to the fold provides a significant boost to what has already been a good defense under Jonathan Gannon, and the offense remains one of the league's most explosive units with Jordan Love targeting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden down the field.Will the Rams hold off the Packers at home, or will Green Bay pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.Where to watch Rams vs. Packers liveDate: Wednesday, Nov. 25 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: SoFi Stadium (Inglewood, California)Streaming: NetflixFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Rams -2.5, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Packers have the ballGreen Bay's offense is entirely based on the passing game because the Packers simply cannot run the ball. Green Bay is last in the league at 3.1 yards per carry. The Packers' 670 rushing yards are 124 fewer than the next-closest team in the league (the Bengals). The Rams allow only 3.9 yards per carry and sport Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald up front. 
The Packers are not going to find success on the ground here — and honestly, they might not even try to do so. They're probably just going to let Jordan Love drop back and let it rip. That's what they've largely done throughout this season, and it's worked quite well for them. Love has completed 63% of his passes at 7.7 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He's ninth in the league in EPA per play, according to Tru Media, thanks largely to the fact that he's created explosives at the fourth-highest rate in the league. When you have Christian Watson and Matthew Golden by your side, that's how the offense is likely going to be built. The Packers really lean into their strengths by having the strong-armed Love target their speedy wideouts with deep routes; Love has thrown 20-plus yards downfield at the second-highest rate in football. The Rams have been the NFL's third-best defense against deep passes this year, according to Tru Media, with opponents completing only 8 of 30 deep passes for 257 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception. The 30 deep passes they've faced are the sixth-fewest in the league. 
It'll be fascinating to see whether Green Bay continues to attack deep downfield or if Love, Watson, Golden and tight end Tucker Kraft instead work the short and intermediate areas of the field that the Rams encourage opposing offenses to throw to because of their coverage structures. It'll also be interesting to see if Trent McDuffie shadows one of the two wideouts or if the Rams play sides with him and Josh Wallace, who has taken the place of the injured Jaylen Watson.L.A. has allowed the league's fewest catches and second-fewest yards to wide receivers this season, according to Pro-Football-Reference, with opposing quarterbacks targeting tight ends and running backs more often than they do against other teams. Tight ends have been targeted at the fourth-highest rate (27.4% of passes, according to Tru Media) against the Rams, while backs have been targeted at the second-highest rate (20.6%). This could be a game where Kraft is more involved in the proceedings. The Packers don't throw to their backs very often because they are not good players, so they'll probably still force the ball to Watson and Golden, even if the Rams do limit wide-receiver production.
When the Rams have the ballIn their first game without all three of Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, the Rams used a highly unusual personnel rotation. Their three leading skill-position players in snaps were all tight ends — and none of those tight ends was the one the Rams drafted in the second round. Their running backs shared the field for 18 snaps after having never previously played together in their careers, according to Tru Media. And one of their two primary wide receivers (rookie sixth-round pick CJ Daniels) played more than seven times as many snaps in Week 10 (44) as he had in his entire career before that (six).PlayerPositionSnapsColby ParkinsonTE52Davis AllenTE51Tyler HigbeeTE50Konata MumpfieldWR47CJ DanielsWR44Kyren WilliamsRB38Blake CorumRB37Ronnie RiversRB17Tutu AtwellWR15Xavier SmithWR9Max KlareTE4Brennan PresleyWR2The Rams were nevertheless able to rack up 436 yards, 28 first downs and 34 points against the decrepit Cardinals' defense. They ran the ball extremely well (202 yards) and were efficient in the passing game, with each of the wideouts creating an explosive play and the backs and tight ends chipping in with short and intermediate grabs. Matthew Stafford threw only 26 passes, but five of them created gains of at least 19 yards, and he averaged nearly 10 yards per attempt.
The Packers, though, are not the Cardinals. Green Bay enters this game allowing the third-fewest net yards per attempt in the league, which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks in addition to passing yards allowed. The Packers have also yielded only 15 touchdowns through the air while intercepting a league-high 14 passes. Their safeties, in particular, have been ballhawks, with Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney combining for nine of those 14 picks and McKinney leading the league with six on his own.Green Bay has been just about average in generating pressure so far this season, recording a sack, hit or hurry on 36.2% of opponent dropbacks, according to Tru Media. (The league average is 36.4% this year.) Getting Parsons back in the fold should help tremendously. He led the NFL in total pressures between 2021 and 2025 despite rushing the passer considerably less often than players like Myles Garrett and Maxx Crosby, who are the only players within 30 pressures of Parsons' total during that span. Parsons will likely play limited snaps, but those snaps should be concentrated on important downs and Matthew Stafford and Co. will need to be aware of where he is at all times.The Packers have also done a pretty strong job of limiting opposing run games, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. The Rams, though, have sported one of the best rushing attacks in the league, with Williams and Corum combining to average 4.6 yards a pop. The offensive line has cleared the way for 1.79 yards before contact per attempt, which is the second-best mark in the league behind only that of the Bills. Williams and Corum (and Ronnie Rivers) also have a combined 21.0% avoided tackle rate, per Tru Media, which is the seventh-best in football.
The Rams will likely have to lean on their run game here to move the ball, because the situation does not line up well for them through the air. The offensive line's ability to dictate the game at the line of scrimmage will likely determine whether they can achieve any degree of offensive success.PredictionThe lift the Packers get from Micah Parsons' return, plus the limitations the Rams' offense should have while working without Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, push me toward Green Bay in this game. I don't foresee the Rams moving the ball as consistently against the Packers as they did against the Cardinals in their first game without all their playmakers. Meanwhile, the Packers have the goods to challenge L.A.'s secondary downfield with Watson and Golden and over the middle with Kraft. Love should be able to get going through the air, even if Green Bay still can't run the ball. Pick: Packers 24, Rams 17

title: Champions League power rankings: Real Madrid claim top spot as Man City, Arsenal, PSG stumble - CBS Sports
body:
1
                                    
                                            Real Madrid
                                        
                                    Hey Jude! The English midfielder may have scored the goal of the year as Jose Mourinho's tweaks worked, taking out his central defense. Madrid responded, scoring five unanswered goals to secure a victory.
                                
                                    1
                                
                                    11-2
                                
                                        2
                                    
                                            Barcelona
                                        
                                    Getting to rest Lamine Yamal and Raphinha while securing a win is a good thing for Barcelona. Their defensive performances with Frenkie De Jong at center back are quite poor, however. As long as this keeps up, it'll be hard to see them as serious UCL contenders.
                                
                                    1
                                
                                    12-1
                                
                                        3
                                    
                                            PSG
                                        
                                    Now without Désiré Doue for the season alongside Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, PSG are slipping from their perch as the team to beat. Luis Enrique is brilliant, but even he can only do so much as he loses a different star each day.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    8-1
                                
                                        4
                                    
                                            Arsenal
                                        
                                    Despite the fact that Victor Gyokeres did score, Arsenal's finishing wasn't good enough as they threw away a game that they should've won. At full health, this may not be an issue, and yes, we're nitpicking when discussing a team that hasn't lost yet in UCL play. But after making the final last year, Arsenal want to win it all, and performances like this one against Dortmund just won't cut it.
                                
                                    --
                                
                                    9-1
                                
                                        5
                                    
                                            Como
                                        
                                    It wasn't pretty, but job done for one of the Champions League's highest-scoring teams in Como. It's good to see a win where Nico Paz isn't involved in the scoring, as it shows that this is a well-rounded squad.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    8-2
                                
                                        6
                                    
                                            Liverpool
                                        
                                    Florian Wirtz may be turning a corner, and with it, so is Liverpool's attack. With a goal contribution for club or country in five consecutive games, he'll have to be gaining confidence at the club, and with that, he's trying more and pulling it off, which is just what the Reds need to reach their full potential.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    6-2
                                
                                        7
                                    
                                            Manchester City
                                        
                                    Scoring may not be an issue for City but transition defense surely is. They allowed both goals to Napoli on the break. If this doesn't improve, City won't advance far in the knockout stages of the competition.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    7-3
                                
                                        8
                                    
                                            Borussia Dortmund
                                        
                                    You know the holiday season has arrived if you're beginning to ask if Borussia Dortmund are for real. Going into London and securing a result without Serhou Guirassy is the kind of thing that says they might be. There's more work to be done, but under Nico Kovac, they're trending in the right direction.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    7-0
                                
                                        9
                                    
                                            Bayern
                                        
                                    This is a battered squad coming into the match withg Harry Kane, Michael Olise, and Luis Diaz all missing from the starting XI. But these depth issues are issues of their own creation, because how can they expect to win a high-level game with outside back Konrad Laimer as your starting striker?
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    6-0
                                
                                        10
                                    
                                            Atletico Madrid
                                        
                                    Julian Alvarez is at least committed to the squad for now, and Atleti are reaping the rewards. A resilient team, they're in this for the long haul as long as everyone can stay healthy.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    10-2
                                
                                        11
                                    
                                            Real Betis
                                        
                                    Cucho Hernandez is back, and Betis are back in the win column. Betis are among the surprise teams in this competition, but their start is legit with four wins in five matches.
                                
                                    --
                                
                                    8-2
                                
                                        12
                                    
                                            Inter
                                        
                                    The Italian side haven't looked like themselves for much of this competition, but handling a dangerous Stuttgart attack will go a long way. Inter only allowed two shots on target in the entire match, controlling it from start to finish.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    9-1
                                
                                        13
                                    
                                            Sporting CP
                                        
                                    Luis Suarez does it again with a brace. Sporting's defense didn't get the job done, conceding penalties and chances left and right in the match. This is still a solid side but the defense has to improve.
                                
                                    6
                                
                                    3-1
                                
                                        14
                                    
                                            Roma
                                        
                                    It was an improvement to turn a UCL lead into a draw instead of a loss. Gian Piero Gasperini's lineup decisions were vindicated with Paulo Dybala and Donyell Malen coming off the bench to make the difference for the squad.
                                
                                    --
                                
                                    9-0
                                
                                        15
                                    
                                            Aston Villa
                                        
                                    What is this team? When Johan Manzambi is at his best, they can beat anyone in the world. But then you'll have games in which Villa can't pass their way out of a paper bag. Unai Emery has to find the middle ground as it feels like an eternity since Villa were a side who won their first three games in Champions League play.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    3-3
                                
                                        16
                                    
                                            Galatasaray
                                        
                                    RAMS Park is a fortress and Aston Villa have become the fourth consecutive English side to fall there. While Galatasaray still have trouble leaving home, this team will be a nightmare bringing their boxing matches to the knockout stage.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    3-2
                                
                                        17
                                    
                                            Fenerbahce
                                        
                                    They should've let manager Ismail Kartal resign the first time he tried because the squad has been on an upward trend in UCL since making the shift at the helm. With an improving defense in front of Ederson, they're going to make things tough.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    2-1
                                
                                        18
                                    
                                            RB Leipzig
                                        
                                    The Antonio Nusa show is in full effect. Leipzig have been a Jekyll-and-Hyde squad in the competition, but with their wings now performing consistently, they're going to trouble some sides.
                                
                                    7
                                
                                    7-3
                                
                                        19
                                    
                                            Stuttgart
                                        
                                    Facing one of the top sides in the UCL shows just how long Stuttgart has to go in this competition. It'll be alright as this squad were never expected to pull up any trees, but it's still a reality check.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    4-5
                                
                                        20
                                    
                                            Club Brugge
                                        
                                    If Nicolo Tresoldi isn't in on the fun, it's a long day for the Belgian squad. Their midfield still isn't up to the standard, but one loss won't break them either.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    3-2
                                
                                        21
                                    
                                            Porto
                                        
                                    A critical victory with some fortune to ride an own goal for the entire match. Sometimes it's better to be lucky than good, as getting back-to-back wins shows that they're going in the right direction.
                                
                                    1
                                
                                        22
                                    
                                            Shakhtar Donetsk
                                        
                                    Needing to play their home games in London due to the ongoing war in Ukraine, it's truly unfortunate that this Shakhtar attack just isn't creating enough. With four goals in five matches, what can change?
                                
                                    1
                                
                                    1-3
                                
                                        23
                                    
                                            Manchester United
                                        
                                    Bruno Fernandes set himself up for success, putting a divot in the pitch that he used to score later in the game. But yet again, more penalties conceded and another red card. Mauricio Pochettino has a tough job ahead of him and no training days to sort it out with United but the squad is still box office.
                                
                                    --
                                
                                    1-5
                                
                                        24
                                    
                                            Napoli
                                        
                                    Finally showing signs of life with Scott McTominay back in the side, Napoli aren't out of the woods yet. But drawing with City will go down as a net positive even if they'll have wanted to win it.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    1-3
                                
                                        25
                                    
                                            PSV
                                        
                                    The Dutch side need to begin picking up points -- and fast. Losing to Madrid happens, so it's going to be about how they respond.
                                
                                    5
                                
                                    1-3
                                
                                        26
                                    
                                            Bodo/Glimt
                                        
                                    Better late than never. For a club like Bodo/Glimt, you have to take advantage of home matches, especially as the weather begins to turn in the Arctic Circle. We're reaching a point where you expect the Norwegian side to get to the knockout stage, which shows the growth of their soccer.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    2-2
                                
                                        27
                                    
                                            Villarreal
                                        
                                    Hanging on by the skin of your teeth still counts. Canadian Tajon Buchanan had an excellent game, but the rest of the squad wasn't up to it.
                                
                                    2
                                
                                    4-6
                                
                                        28
                                    
                                            Lille
                                        
                                    What a time for Davide Ancelotti's first Champions League win. Sure, Bayern Munich weren't at their best, but his squad were able to keep belief and push for a victory. It's still a long way to the top 24, but this is a step in the right direction.
                                
                                    7
                                
                                    6-2
                                
                                        29
                                    
                                            LASK
                                        
                                    The goals dried up at a time when they couldn't afford for them to. LASK can still move on from this loss but these are the kind of games that they need to win.
                                
                                    5
                                
                                    2-3
                                
                                        30
                                    
                                            Feyenoord
                                        
                                    At least they got a win in this competition, because who knows when the next one is coming. Porto have been poor and the Dutch side couldn't even handle them as they find themselves in a tough place.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    1-4
                                
                                        31
                                    
                                            Viking
                                        
                                    The Norwegian side will always have their draw against Bayern Munich to look back on, as it has been rough sledding since in this competition.
                                
                                    1
                                
                                    1-3
                                
                                        32
                                    
                                            Sabah
                                        
                                    They played Barcelona, scored a goal, and didn't lose by six, so that's something.
                                
                                    1
                                
                                        33
                                    
                                            AEK Athens
                                        
                                    They've been in games, which is good, but those aren't turning into the wins that are needed to stay in the competition. AEK are firmly moving into the "happy to be here" category.
                                
                                    1
                                
                                    1-4
                                
                                        34
                                    
                                            Slavia Praha
                                        
                                    The attack was going to struggle without Lucas Provod, but they had their chances and weren't able to take them while VAR popped up everywhere.
                                
                                    1
                                
                                    0-4
                                
                                        35
                                    
                                            Lens
                                        
                                    It doesn't matter who the manager is -- this team is a shell of the one that pushed PSG for the league title last campaign. I would say see you next season, but as things stand, it's unlikely that Lens will be back in European play next year.
                                
                                    3
                                
                                    4-5
                                
                                        36
                                    
                                            Slovan Bratislava
                                        
                                    On the bright side, Yaya Toure is now overseeing the joint worst UCL defense (alongside Lens) instead of the worst with 19 goals conceded. It's about the little things.
                                
                                    --
                                
                                    0-5

Happy Thanksgiving! This is the perfect week to post up at the in-laws and watch plenty of college basketball. Wednesday's slate is loaded with outstanding games from morning till the wee hours of the night. 


This is the time of year when all the preseason optimism can go away in a hurry. Beating up on lesser competition in non-conference play is all fun and games. This is the meat and potatoes where the big dawgs go toe-to-toe. Strengths and weaknesses will be on full display. 


Let's dive into predictions for the top games on Wednesday's slate.

 No. 10 UConn vs. No. 16 Duke 


	7 p.m. on Amazon Prime: Arizona used an interesting recipe to beat UConn 85-79 Wednesday that Duke could be in position to replicate. The Wildcats chose to top-lock a bunch of UConn's off-ball screens to try and blow up the action and funnel everything toward shot-blocker Motiejus Krivas in the middle of the floor. Duke can do that too, with big man Patrick Ngongba holding down the fort on the back end. He has to avoid foul trouble, but Duke has the size, strength and length on the perimeter with Caleb Foster, Dame Sarr and Sebastian Wilkins to give some of UConn's shooters some issues.  


Turning defense into offense has to be the recipe for Duke because I don't think this offense is in a great position right now to score against a set UConn halfcourt defense. Silas Demary Jr. and Jayden Ross are just way too good defensively, and Duke hasn't found the right mix offensively. That said, Duke is due to make some shots, and it's the deeper, bigger team. Plus, UConn big man Na'jai Hines seems to always be in foul trouble. If that happens, Duke is going to salt this one away. The Khamenia injury looms large.
